clue.text: His duties are of a light character, albeit colourful

definitions.text: His duties are of a light character, albeit colourful

parts.words: His duties are of a light character, albeit colourful
parts.note: reads like a description of a cheerful, easy-going job, but the light is a railway lamp showing red or green

explanation.definitionFit: A railway worker in a box sets the coloured lamps that tell train drivers to stop or go.

clue.text: Big hit at court

parts.note: a hit show is a runaway success, and the hard overhead shot on a tennis court has the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A runaway theatre success and a hard downward tennis stroke share one name.

clue.text: It provides a precarious perch-or material for a good stick

definitions.meaning: being 'up a tree' of this kind is the idiom for being stuck in difficulties
the tree yields a sticky resin, so it supplies adhesive

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'up a gum tree' means in a fix, and the eucalyptus oozes a resin usable as glue.

clue.text: Also the worker takes in nothing with this movement

parts.note: also means and
the ant is the crossword's stock worker
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A labourer pauses a concert piece, taking in nothing more of the music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' is the musical sense: a section of a symphony, here one marked slightly faster than andante.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece or section to be played at a moderately slow, walking pace is a musical movement.

clue.text: Homoeopathic cure for yellow fever ?

parts.note: homoeopathy treats like with like, so a yellow fever would be treated by soaking in something yellow

explanation.definitionFit: A hot foot-soak with the yellow condiment was an old household remedy for colds and chills.

clue.text: Present from some unknown admirer

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow, here buried in the middle of unknown

explanation.surface: A gift arrives anonymously from a secret admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the adjective-turned-adverb sense, at this moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The present moment is the time happening at this very instant.

clue.text: A crack in a cracker

parts.note: a crack is a wisecrack, and a Christmas cracker holds a slip of paper with a witty saying

explanation.definitionFit: The slip of paper inside a Christmas cracker carries a short saying or joke.

clue.text: They give help in writing

indicators.note: in tells us the word for help is placed inside the abbreviation for writing

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
help means aid

explanation.surface: Secretaries or assistants support someone with their correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: This is an &lit: the whole clue is both definition and wordplay, since housemaids are the ones who give help.
explanation.definitionFit: Housemaids and ladies' maids are servants whose job is to assist.

clue.text: It'll teach you to get out in it anyway !

indicators.note: anyway means arranged in any fashion, so the letters of out in it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A coach promises lessons in getting yourself out of a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' rearranges OUT IN IT; 'to get' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching or instruction given to pupils.

clue.text: They don't stop playing — or do they?

definitions.text: They don't stop playing — or do they?

parts.words: They don't stop playing — or do they?
parts.note: reads as tireless performers, but the instrument's stops are the knobs these players pull

explanation.definitionFit: Church keyboard players pull stops to choose the pipe ranks that sound.

clue.text: Men-of-war embrace Ada!

annotationWithheld.why: Men-of-war embrace Ada! (7): ARMADAS is ARMS round ADA, but 'embrace' must both give ARMS and signal the container, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Concoction of gin with fish

indicators.note: a concoction is a mixture made up from ingredients, so the letters of gin and with are mixed

explanation.surface: A cocktail of gin served alongside a fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: The newspaper text read 'gun', but the page prints 'gin', and GIN plus WITH rearranged gives the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The whiting is a small sea fish of the cod family.

clue.text: Let her get on with the bird

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave a woman to carry on with her pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let' and 'get' and 'with' are just joining words; the pieces are the clue's own her and on.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Being taken in by a confession

definitions.meaning: entry, being let into a place

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both entrance into a venue and an acknowledgment of guilt.

clue.text: They make the most of the minute

definitions.text: They make the most of the minute

parts.words: They make the most of the minute
parts.note: reads as people who use their time well, but minute is the adjective for tiny things, which these instruments magnify

explanation.definitionFit: Laboratory magnifiers enlarge tiny objects for viewing.

clue.text: It is, indeed, a natural flower

indicators.note: it is in the next word, so the short run is lifted from the middle of indeed

explanation.surface: Someone insists a bloom is truly a wild one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is the crossword's 'something that flows', a river; this one runs in Scotland and also between England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a natural watercourse, and the Dee is one in Britain.

clue.text: He needs no encouragement to hang on

definitions.text: He needs no encouragement to hang on

parts.words: He needs no encouragement to hang on
parts.note: sounds like someone persistent, but it describes a person who relies on another for support

explanation.definitionFit: A person supported by another, financially or otherwise, relies on them.

clue.text: They should give good reasons for trying

definitions.text: They should give good reasons for trying

parts.words: They should give good reasons for trying
parts.note: sounds like motivation to make an effort, but trying is putting someone on trial in court

explanation.definitionFit: Formal charges laid before a court set out why a defendant is to be tried.

clue.text: Nice smart sort of ruffian

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to arrange, so the letters of nice smart are rearranged

explanation.surface: A well-dressed, pleasant type turns out to be a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges NICE SMART; the surface makes it sound like a description of the ruffian.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain or wrongdoer is a ruffian of the worst kind.

clue.text: If efficient, they should give no grounds for complaint

definitions.text: If efficient, they should give no grounds for complaint

parts.words: If efficient, they should give no grounds for complaint
parts.note: reads as well-run services, but grounds are coffee dregs a good coffee-maker filters out

explanation.definitionFit: Coffee pots that drip water through ground beans keep the dregs out of the cup.

clue.text: Topping kind of felt

definitions.meaning: the covering put on top of a building
the tarred fabric laid under tiles is named for this

explanation.definitionFit: Material covering a house top, and the bitumen felt used there, share the name.

clue.text: Island haven of vegetarians?

definitions.meaning: a Greek island in the Dodecanese, also spelt Kos
a lettuce, with the question mark admitting the stretch from salad to refuge

explanation.definitionFit: A Greek island and a long-leaved lettuce share the name.

clue.text: Nautical roundabout

parts.note: sounds like a seaside fairground ride, but describes a revolving drum on a ship's deck

explanation.definitionFit: A ship's winch turns around a vertical axis, pushed by sailors walking in a circle.

clue.text: New sermon-material for one of the Ages of Man ?

definitions.text: one of the Ages of Man ?

parts.note: neo- is the prefix meaning new
As You Like It finds 'sermons in stones', so stone is sermon material, and lithic means made of stone

explanation.surface: A fresh supply of preaching material for a stage of life, from Shakespeare's seven ages.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves echo As You Like It: 'sermons in stones' and the 'seven ages' speech. The Ages here are the archaeologists' periods of prehistory instead.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Stone Age is a prehistoric period of humanity, when farming began.

clue.text: Goes in three times for an exam

parts.note: ter is Latin for three times, used in prescriptions and music

explanation.surface: A student resits a test for the third time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Inter was the intermediate examination, once sat midway through a London University degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for the intermediate examination taken partway through a degree course.

clue.text: Tricky poser could tie anyone up

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for cords that could bind someone

indicators.note: tricky means the letters of poser are handled in a tricky, rearranged way

explanation.surface: A hard puzzle could leave anyone tied in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' rearranges POSER. The definition describes what the cords do.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengths of cord are used to bind and secure people or things.

clue.text: Suiting a Russian, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a hard-wearing twill cloth made into suits
a man's name common in Russia, as in the impresario Diaghilev

explanation.definitionFit: A twilled worsted cloth for suits, and a first name borne by many Russians.

clue.text: But flyovers are not designed for him

definitions.text: But flyovers are not designed for him

parts.words: But flyovers are not designed for him
parts.note: flyovers are road bridges for cars, though the word suggests something meant for one who flies over

explanation.definitionFit: A pilot flies aircraft, so he alone truly flies over things.

clue.text: Level up or knock down

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for level is read from bottom to top

parts.note: level means par, on a par

explanation.surface: Raise the standard or else tear it all down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PAR backwards; 'down' merely closes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp tap or blow on a door is a knock.

clue.text: Given a licking by Jack and his missus

definitions.text: Given a licking by Jack and his missus

parts.words: Given a licking by Jack and his missus
parts.note: a licking sounds like a beating, but in the nursery rhyme Jack Sprat and his wife licked their dish clean

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme ends 'And so between them both, you see, they licked the platter clean.'
explanation.definitionFit: A large flat serving plate is what the couple in the nursery rhyme cleaned.

clue.text: One whose master went to Aleppo, said the first witch

definitions.text: One whose master went to Aleppo, said the first witch

parts.words: One whose master went to Aleppo, said the first witch
parts.note: in Macbeth the First Witch says of a sailor 'Her husband's to Aleppo gone, master o' the' ship of this name

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare names the sailor's ship after the striped big cat.

clue.text: Overtime for the grammarian ?

parts.note: overtime is split as over and time: over means gone by, and a grammarian's word for time is a verb form

explanation.definitionFit: A grammarian's term for the verb form that places an action earlier.
